notes: The parts list marked the board as not in the catalogue, but the circuit is an Arduino Leonardo and the catalogue has arduino-leonardo, so I used that type.
The pushbutton straddles the breadboard centre gap. Its legs are in columns 4 and 6. The image's top half (rows j to f) is the catalogue's 'b' bank, and its bottom half (rows e to a) is the 't' bank.

I took the pushbutton's two joined sides to be its left (column 4) and right (column 6) leg pairs. So 1.l and 1.r are the column-4 legs (4b.f and 4t.e), and 2.l and 2.r are the column-6 legs (6b.f and 6t.e). Pressing the button joins column 4 to column 6.
The blue wire runs from pin 2 to column 6 (hole 6b.i), which is the button's pin-2 side.
The black wire runs from a GND header pin to hole 4t.c in column 4, which is the button's ground side. I assumed the GND.1 port for the header pin shown next to 5V.
There is no external pull-up resistor. The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so the internal pull-up is used.
